raw: CHAPTER XI. A Companion Picture
en: [Chapter 11] A Companion Picture

raw: “Sydney,” said Mr.
en: "Sydney," Mr.
ko: "시드니,"

raw: Stryver, on that self-same night, or morning, to his jackal; “mix another bowl of punch; I have something to say to you.”
en: Stryver said to his assistant on that same night, or rather morning, "mix another bowl of punch. I have something to tell you."
ko: 스트라이버가 바로 그날 밤, 아니 새벽에 그의 조수에게 말했다. "펀치를 한 그릇 더 섞어주게. 자네에게 할 말이 있네."

raw: Sydney had been working double tides that night, and the night before, and the night before that, and a good many nights in succession, making a grand clearance among Mr.
en: Sydney had been working double shifts that night, the night before, and for many nights in a row, clearing out Mr.
ko: 시드니는 그날 밤, 전날 밤, 그리고 며칠 밤을 연이어 두 배로 일하며 정리를 하고 있었다,

raw: Stryver’s papers before the setting in of the long vacation.
en: Stryver's legal papers before the start of the summer court vacation.
ko: 여름 법정 휴가 기간이 시작되기 전에 스트라이버의 법률 서류들을 말이다.

raw: The clearance was effected at last; the Stryver arrears were handsomely fetched up; everything was got rid of until November should come with its fogs atmospheric, and fogs legal, and bring grist to the mill again.
en: The work was finally done. Stryver’s backlogged cases were completely caught up, leaving everything clear until November when the winter weather and new legal cases would bring work back again.
ko: 마침내 일이 끝났다. 스트라이버의 밀려 있던 사건들은 완전히 처리되었고, 겨울 날씨와 새로운 법적 사건들이 다시 일을 몰고 올 십일월까지 모든 것이 깨끗하게 정리되었다.

raw: Sydney was none the livelier and none the soberer for so much application.
en: Sydney was neither more energetic nor more sober for all his hard work.
ko: 시드니는 그의 모든 고된 노동에도 불구하고 활기가 넘치지도 더 제정신이지도 않았다.

raw: It had taken a deal of extra wet-towelling to pull him through the night; a correspondingly extra quantity of wine had preceded the towelling; and he was in a very damaged condition, as he now pulled his turban off and threw it into the basin in which he had steeped it at intervals for the last six hours.
en: It had taken extra wet towels wrapped around his head to get him through the night, preceded by a large amount of wine. He looked in very poor shape as he took his makeshift turban off and threw it into the basin of water where he had been soaking it for the last six hours.
ko: 그가 밤을 지새우기 위해 머리에 여분의 젖은 수건을 둘러야 했고, 그 전에는 많은 양의 와인을 마셨다. 그는 지난 여섯 시간 동안 적셔둔 임시 터번을 벗어 물동이에 던져 넣을 때 매우 초라해 보였다.

raw: “Are you mixing that other bowl of punch?” said Stryver the portly, with his hands in his waistband, glancing round from the sofa where he lay on his back.
en: "Are you mixing that other bowl of punch?" the portly Stryver asked, lying on his back on the sofa with his hands on his belt.
ko: "그 다른 펀치 그릇을 섞고 있나?" 뚱뚱한 스트라이버가 두 손을 벨트에 얹은 채 소파에 누워 물었다.

raw: “I am.”
en: "I am."
ko: "그러고 있습니다."

raw: “Now, look here!
en: "Now, look here!
ko: "자, 이봐!

raw: I am going to tell you something that will rather surprise you, and that perhaps will make you think me not quite as shrewd as you usually do think me.
en: I am going to tell you something that will surprise you, and might make you think I'm not as clever as you usually believe.
ko: 자네를 놀라게 할 만한 말을 하려고 하는데, 어쩌면 내가 평소 자네가 믿는 것만큼 똑똑하지 않다고 생각하게 만들지도 모르겠군.

raw: I intend to marry.”
en: I plan to marry."
ko: 난 결혼할 계획이라네."

raw: “_Do_ you?”
en: "Do you?"
ko: "그러십니까?"

raw: “Yes.
en: "Yes.
ko: "그렇다네.

raw: And not for money.
en: And not for money.
ko: 돈 때문이 아니라네.

raw: What do you say now?”
en: What do you say to that?"
ko: 이에 대해 어떻게 생각하나?"

raw: “I don’t feel disposed to say much.
en: "I don't have much to say.
ko: "별로 할 말이 없군요.

raw: Who is she?”
en: Who is she?"
ko: 그녀는 누구입니까?"

raw: “Guess.”
en: "Guess."
ko: "맞혀보게."

raw: “Do I know her?”
en: "Do I know her?"
ko: "제가 아는 분입니까?"

raw: “Guess.”
en: "Guess."
ko: "맞혀보라니까."

raw: “I am not going to guess, at five o’clock in the morning, with my brains frying and sputtering in my head.
en: "I am not guessing at five o'clock in the morning, with my brain fried and exhausted.
ko: "뇌가 다 타버리고 지쳐버린 새벽 다섯 시에는 추측하고 싶지 않습니다.

raw: If you want me to guess, you must ask me to dinner.”
en: If you want me to guess, you'll have to invite me to dinner."
ko: 제가 추측하기를 원하신다면, 저를 저녁 식사에 초대하셔야 할 겁니다."

raw: “Well then, I’ll tell you,” said Stryver, coming slowly into a sitting posture. “Sydney, I rather despair of making myself intelligible to you, because you are such an insensible dog.”
en: "Well, then, I'll tell you," said Stryver, slowly sitting up. "Sydney, I despair of explaining this to you, because you are such an unfeeling dog."
ko: "음, 그렇다면 말해주지." 스트라이버가 천천히 일어나 앉으며 말했다. "시드니, 자네는 정말 무정한 녀석이라서 이것을 자네에게 설명할 생각을 하니 절망적이군."

raw: “And you,” returned Sydney, busy concocting the punch, “are such a sensitive and poetical spirit--”
en: "And you," Sydney replied, busy mixing the punch, "are such a sensitive and romantic soul."
ko: "그리고 선생님께서는," 펀치를 섞느라 바쁜 시드니가 대답했다. "참으로 예민하고 낭만적인 영혼이시죠."

raw: “Come!” rejoined Stryver, laughing boastfully, “though I don’t prefer any claim to being the soul of Romance (for I hope I know better), still I am a tenderer sort of fellow than _you_.”
en: "Come on!" Stryver laughed boastfully. "While I don't claim to be a romantic hero, I am still a much warmer person than _you_."
ko: "이봐!" 스트라이버가 거들먹거리며 웃었다. "내가 낭만적인 영웅이라고 주장하지는 않지만, 그래도 내가 자네보다는 훨씬 따뜻한 사람이지."

raw: “You are a luckier, if you mean that.”
en: "You are luckier, if that's what you mean."
ko: "선생님이 더 운이 좋으시죠, 그런 뜻이시라면요."

raw: “I don’t mean that.
en: "I don't mean that.
ko: "그런 뜻이 아니네.

raw: I mean I am a man of more--more--”
en: I mean I am a man of more, more, "
ko: 내 말은 내가 훨씬 더, 더, "

raw: “Say gallantry, while you are about it,” suggested Carton.
en: "Say gallantry, while you're at it," Carton suggested.
ko: "이왕 말하는 김에 정중함이라고 하시죠." 카턴이 제안했다.

raw: “Well! I’ll say gallantry.
en: "Well, I'll say gallantry.
ko: "그래, 정중함이라고 해두지.

raw: My meaning is that I am a man,” said Stryver, inflating himself at his friend as he made the punch, “who cares more to be agreeable, who takes more pains to be agreeable, who knows better how to be agreeable, in a woman’s society, than you do.”
en: I mean that I am a man," Stryver said, looking proudly at his friend, "who cares more about being pleasant, who takes more trouble to be pleasant, and who knows better how to behave in a woman's company than you do."
ko: 내 말은 말이야," 스트라이버가 친구를 자랑스럽게 쳐다보며 말했다, "내가 자네보다 기분 좋은 사람이 되는 것에 더 신경을 쓰고, 그러기 위해 더 많은 수고를 하며, 여자들과 함께 있을 때 어떻게 행동해야 하는지 더 잘 아는 남자라는 거지."

raw: “Go on,” said Sydney Carton.
en: "Go on," said Sydney Carton.
ko: "계속하시죠." 시드니 카턴이 말했다.

raw: “No; but before I go on,” said Stryver, shaking his head in his bullying way, “I’ll have this out with you.
en: "No, but before I continue," Stryver said, shaking his head in his usual bullying way, "I want to settle this with you.
ko: "아니, 하지만 내가 계속하기 전에," 스트라이버가 평소의 위압적인 방식으로 고개를 저으며 말했다, "자네와 이 문제를 확실히 짚고 넘어가고 싶군.

raw: You’ve been at Doctor Manette’s house as much as I have, or more than I have.
en: You've been to Doctor Manette's house as much as I have, or more.
ko: 자네도 나만큼, 혹은 나보다 더 많이 마네트 의사의 집에 갔지.

raw: Why, I have been ashamed of your moroseness there!
en: I have actually been embarrassed by your behavior there!
ko: 나는 사실 거기서 자네의 행동 때문에 당황스러웠다네!

raw: Your manners have been of that silent and sullen and hangdog kind, that, upon my life and soul, I have been ashamed of you, Sydney!”
en: You sit there silent and gloomy. I've been ashamed of your manners, Sydney!"
ko: 자네는 조용하고 우울하게 앉아만 있지. 나는 자네의 태도가 부끄러웠다네, 시드니!"

raw: “It should be very beneficial to a man in your practice at the bar, to be ashamed of anything,” returned Sydney; “you ought to be much obliged to me.”
en: "It must be very useful for a lawyer like you to feel ashamed of anything," Sydney replied. "You should thank me."
ko: "선생님 같은 변호사가 무언가에 대해 부끄러움을 느낄 수 있다는 건 매우 유용한 일이 틀림없습니다." 시드니가 대답했다. "저에게 감사하셔야 합니다."

raw: “You shall not get off in that way,” rejoined Stryver, shouldering the rejoinder at him; “no, Sydney, it’s my duty to tell you--and I tell you to your face to do you good--that you are a devilish ill-conditioned fellow in that sort of society.
en: "You won't get out of it that way," Stryver argued. "No, Sydney, it's my duty to tell you, and I tell you to your face for your own good, that you are a very unpleasant fellow in social gatherings.
ko: "그런 식으로 빠져나갈 순 없을 거다." 스트라이버가 따졌다. "아니, 시드니, 자네에게 말하는 것이 내 의무이고, 자네를 위해 자네 면전에서 말하는 건데, 자네는 사교 모임에서 매우 불쾌한 녀석이야.

raw: You are a disagreeable fellow.”
en: You are disagreeable."
ko: 자네는 무례하다고."

raw: Sydney drank a bumper of the punch he had made, and laughed.
en: Sydney drank a large glass of the punch he had made and laughed.
ko: 시드니는 자신이 만든 펀치를 큰 잔으로 마시며 웃었다.

raw: “Look at me!” said Stryver, squaring himself; “I have less need to make myself agreeable than you have, being more independent in circumstances.
en: "Look at me!" Stryver said, squaring his shoulders. "I have less need to be polite than you do, since I am wealthier and more independent.
ko: "나를 보게!" 스트라이버가 어깨를 쫙 펴며 말했다. "나는 자네보다 돈도 많고 독립적이니 자네만큼 예의 바를 필요가 없다네.

raw: Why do I do it?”
en: Why do I do it?"
ko: 그런데 왜 내가 그렇게 하겠나?"

raw: “I never saw you do it yet,” muttered Carton.
en: "I've never seen you do it yet," Carton muttered.
ko: "아직 그러시는 걸 본 적이 없습니다만." 카턴이 중얼거렸다.

raw: “I do it because it’s politic; I do it on principle.
en: "I do it because it is smart business; I do it on principle.
ko: "영리한 일이기 때문에 그렇게 하는 것이지. 원칙에 따라 하는 거네.

raw: And look at me!
en: And look at me!
ko: 그리고 나를 보라고!

raw: I get on.”
en: I succeed."
ko: 나는 성공하잖아."

raw: “You don’t get on with your account of your matrimonial intentions,”  answered Carton, with a careless air; “I wish you would keep to that.
en: "You aren't succeeding in telling me about your marriage plans," Carton answered carelessly. "I wish you would stick to that.
ko: "선생님의 결혼 계획에 대해 제게 말씀하시는 건 성공하지 못하고 계시군요." 카턴이 무심하게 대답했다. "그 이야기에만 집중하셨으면 좋겠는데요.

raw: As to me--will you never understand that I am incorrigible?”
en: As for me, will you never understand that I cannot be reformed?"
ko: 저로 말씀드리자면, 제가 교화될 수 없다는 것을 영원히 이해하지 못하실 겁니까?"

raw: He asked the question with some appearance of scorn.
en: He asked the question with a hint of scorn.
ko: 그는 경멸조로 질문을 던졌다.

raw: “You have no business to be incorrigible,” was his friend’s answer, delivered in no very soothing tone.
en: "You have no right to be unreformed," his friend answered sharply.
ko: "자네는 교화되지 않을 권리가 없다네." 그의 친구가 날카롭게 대답했다.

raw: “I have no business to be, at all, that I know of,” said Sydney Carton. “Who is the lady?”
en: "I have no right to exist at all, as far as I know," said Sydney Carton. "Who is the lady?"
ko: "제가 아는 한, 저에게는 애초에 존재할 권리가 없습니다." 시드니 카턴이 말했다. "그 부인은 누구십니까?"

raw: “Now, don’t let my announcement of the name make you uncomfortable, Sydney,” said Mr.
en: "Now, don't let the name make you uncomfortable, Sydney," Mr.
ko: "자, 그 이름 때문에 불편해하지는 말게, 시드니,"

raw: Stryver, preparing him with ostentatious friendliness for the disclosure he was about to make, “because I know you don’t mean half you say; and if you meant it all, it would be of no importance.
en: Stryver said, preparing him with a show of friendliness. "I know you don't mean half of what you say, and even if you did, it wouldn't matter.
ko: 스트라이버가 친근함을 과시하며 그를 준비시키며 말했다. "나는 자네가 말하는 것의 절반은 진심이 아니라는 것을 알고, 설령 진심이라 해도 상관없지.

raw: I make this little preface, because you once mentioned the young lady to me in slighting terms.”
en: I say this because you once spoke of the young lady in a dismissive way."
ko: 내가 이 말을 하는 이유는 자네가 예전에 그 젊은 숙녀에 대해 무시하는 투로 말한 적이 있기 때문이네."

raw: “I did?”
en: "I did?"
ko: "제가 그랬습니까?"

raw: “Certainly; and in these chambers.”
en: "Certainly, right here in these offices."
ko: "물론이지, 바로 여기 이 사무실에서 말이야."

raw: Sydney Carton looked at his punch and looked at his complacent friend; drank his punch and looked at his complacent friend.
en: Sydney Carton looked at his drink, then at his smug friend. He drank and looked at him again.
ko: 시드니 카턴은 자신의 술잔을 보더니 이내 우쭐대는 친구를 바라보았다. 그는 술을 마시고 다시 그를 쳐다보았다.

raw: “You made mention of the young lady as a golden-haired doll.
en: "You called the young lady a golden-haired doll.
ko: "자네는 그 젊은 숙녀를 금발의 인형이라고 불렀지.

raw: The young lady is Miss Manette.
en: The lady is Miss Manette.
ko: 그 숙녀는 마네트 양이네.

raw: If you had been a fellow of any sensitiveness or delicacy of feeling in that kind of way, Sydney, I might have been a little resentful of your employing such a designation; but you are not.
en: If you were a sensitive fellow, Sydney, I might be angry with you for using such a term, but you aren't.
ko: 만약 자네가 예민한 녀석이었다면, 시드니, 자네가 그런 표현을 쓴 것에 대해 화를 냈을지도 모르지만, 자네는 그렇지 않으니까.

raw: You want that sense altogether; therefore I am no more annoyed when I think of the expression, than I should be annoyed by a man’s opinion of a picture of mine, who had no eye for pictures: or of a piece of music of mine, who had no ear for music.”
en: You lack that sensitivity entirely. Therefore, I am no more annoyed by your opinion than I would be by a blind man's opinion of my painting, or a deaf man's opinion of my music."
ko: 자네는 그런 예민함이 전혀 없지. 그러므로 장님이 내 그림을 평가하거나 귀머거리가 내 음악을 평가할 때 짜증이 나지 않는 것처럼, 자네의 의견에도 조금도 화가 나지 않는다네."

raw: Sydney Carton drank the punch at a great rate; drank it by bumpers, looking at his friend.
en: Sydney Carton drank the punch quickly, glass after glass, staring at his friend.
ko: 시드니 카턴은 친구를 응시하며 펀치를 연거푸 재빨리 들이켰다.

raw: “Now you know all about it, Syd,” said Mr.
en: "Now you know all about it, Syd," Mr.
ko: "이제 자네도 모든 걸 알게 되었군, 시드."

raw: Stryver. “I don’t care about fortune: she is a charming creature, and I have made up my mind to please myself: on the whole, I think I can afford to please myself.
en: Stryver said. "I don't care about a fortune. She is a charming girl, and I have decided to please myself. On the whole, I think I can afford to please myself.
ko: 스트라이버가 말했다. "나는 재산에는 관심이 없어. 그녀는 매력적인 소녀고, 나는 나 자신을 기쁘게 하기로 결정했지. 대체로 나는 나 자신을 기쁘게 할 여유가 있다고 생각한다네.

raw: She will have in me a man already pretty well off, and a rapidly rising man, and a man of some distinction: it is a piece of good fortune for her, but she is worthy of good fortune.
en: In me, she will have a wealthy husband, a rapidly rising lawyer, and a man of distinction. It is a great opportunity for her, and she deserves it.
ko: 내 안에서 그녀는 부유한 남편, 빠르게 출세하는 변호사, 그리고 명망 있는 사람을 얻게 될 걸세. 이것은 그녀에게 엄청난 기회이며, 그녀는 그럴 자격이 있어.

raw: Are you astonished?”
en: Are you surprised?"
ko: 놀랐나?"

raw: Carton, still drinking the punch, rejoined, “Why should I be astonished?”
en: Carton, still drinking, replied, "Why should I be surprised?"
ko: 카턴은 여전히 술을 마시며 대답했다. "내가 왜 놀라야 합니까?"

raw: “You approve?”
en: "Do you approve?"
ko: "자네는 찬성하는가?"

raw: Carton, still drinking the punch, rejoined, “Why should I not approve?”
en: Carton, still drinking, replied, "Why should I not approve?"
ko: 카턴은 여전히 술을 마시며 대답했다. "내가 왜 찬성하지 않겠습니까?"

raw: “Well!” said his friend Stryver, “you take it more easily than I fancied you would, and are less mercenary on my behalf than I thought you would be; though, to be sure, you know well enough by this time that your ancient chum is a man of a pretty strong will.
en: "Well!" said Stryver. "You take it more easily than I expected, and you aren't as greedy on my behalf as I thought you would be. Though you know by now that your old friend has a strong will.
ko: "음!" 스트라이버가 말했다. "자네는 내 예상보다 더 쉽게 받아들이는군. 그리고 내가 생각했던 것만큼 나를 위해 욕심을 내지도 않고 말이야. 비록 자네의 오랜 친구가 강한 의지를 가지고 있다는 것은 이제 자네도 알겠지만."

raw: Yes, Sydney, I have had enough of this style of life, with no other as a change from it; I feel that it is a pleasant thing for a man to have a home when he feels inclined to go to it (when he doesn’t, he can stay away), and I feel that Miss Manette will tell well in any station, and will always do me credit.
en: Yes, Sydney, I have had enough of this bachelor life. It is nice for a man to have a home to go to when he wants, and when he doesn't, he can stay away. I think Miss Manette will look good in high society and will always do me credit.
ko: 그래, 시드니, 난 이 독신 생활에 질렸어. 남자가 원할 때 돌아갈 수 있는 집이 있고, 원하지 않을 때는 떨어져 있을 수 있다는 건 좋은 일이지. 내 생각에 마네트 양은 상류 사회에 잘 어울릴 것이고 항상 나를 빛내줄 거야.

raw: So I have made up my mind.
en: So I have made up my mind.
ko: 그래서 나는 결심했네.

raw: And now, Sydney, old boy, I want to say a word to _you_ about _your_ prospects.
en: And now, Sydney, I want to give _you_ some advice about _your_ future.
ko: 그리고 이제, 시드니, 나는 '자네'의 미래에 대해 '자네'에게 조언을 좀 해주고 싶네.

raw: You are in a bad way, you know; you really are in a bad way.
en: You are in a bad way, you know.
ko: 자네 상황이 좋지 않다는 건, 자네도 알 거야.

raw: You don’t know the value of money, you live hard, you’ll knock up one of these days, and be ill and poor; you really ought to think about a nurse.”
en: You don't know the value of money, you live too hard, and you will ruin your health one day and end up sick and poor. You really ought to find a wife to look after you."
ko: 자네는 돈의 가치를 모르고, 너무 험하게 살고 있어. 언젠가 건강을 망치고 병들고 가난해질 거야. 자네를 돌봐줄 아내를 꼭 찾아야 해."

raw: The prosperous patronage with which he said it, made him look twice as big as he was, and four times as offensive.
en: The smug, patronizing tone in which he spoke made him look twice as big and far more offensive.
ko: 그가 말하는 우쭐대고 선심 쓰는 듯한 말투는 그를 두 배나 더 커 보이게 했고 훨씬 더 불쾌하게 만들었다.

raw: “Now, let me recommend you,” pursued Stryver, “to look it in the face.
en: Stryver continued, "Let me recommend you to face the facts.
ko: 스트라이버가 계속했다. "자네에게 현실을 직시하라고 권하고 싶네.

raw: I have looked it in the face, in my different way; look it in the face, you, in your different way.
en: I have faced them in my own way; you should do the same.
ko: 나는 나만의 방식으로 현실을 마주했어. 자네도 그래야 해.

raw: Marry.
en: Marry.
ko: 결혼하게.

raw: Provide somebody to take care of you.
en: Find someone to take care of you.
ko: 자네를 돌봐줄 사람을 찾게.

raw: Never mind your having no enjoyment of women’s society, nor understanding of it, nor tact for it.
en: Don't worry that you don't understand women or have no social skills.
ko: 여자를 이해하지 못한다거나 사교성이 없다고 걱정하지 말게.

raw: Find out somebody.
en: Just find someone.
ko: 그저 누군가를 찾게.

raw: Find out some respectable woman with a little property--somebody in the landlady way, or lodging-letting way--and marry her, against a rainy day. That’s the kind of thing for _you_.
en: Find a respectable woman with a little money, perhaps a landlady or someone who lets lodgings, and marry her to secure your future.
ko: 돈이 좀 있는 존경할 만한 여자, 아마도 여주인이나 하숙을 치는 사람을 찾아서 그녀와 결혼하여 자네의 미래를 보장받게.

raw: Now think of it, Sydney.”
en: Think about it, Sydney."
ko: 생각해 보게, 시드니."

raw: “I’ll think of it,” said Sydney.
en: "I'll think of it," said Sydney.
ko: "생각해 보죠," 시드니가 말했다.
